I went to collect my prescription from the pharmacy, but they told me it wasn't available yet. So, I decided to call the next day (Thursday), but there was no answer. Frustrated, I contacted my GP and the receptionist told me that the issue was between me and the pharmacy, as they had supposedly sent the prescription there. Let me explain my last visit to the GP. They were still using paper prescriptions at that time. have been using Gill Medical Service for three years now, and I have never experienced such inconvenience as I have recently. I understand that a new woman - Asian lady - has recently joined the reception team, and her manner of dealing with patients has been unacceptable.

My doctor instructed me to book a blood test within a specific time frame—by July 23rd, to be exact. Despite available booking slots, she falsely claimed there were none. When I began to insist that I needed to follow the doctor's instructions, suddenly a slot became available. This was clearly dishonest and highly unprofessional.

In addition, when I asked her about adding certain tests to the blood work, she insisted I speak to the doctor first, even though the tests could have been added after consultation with the reception, as has been done before. She made me book an unnecessary slot, wasting an appointment time that could have gone to someone else.

Thankfully, another receptionist—blonde-haired—stepped in via phone and resolved the issue professionally.

I strongly believe this individual - the new lady should not be working at the GP practice. If she doesn’t understand her responsibilities, she should at least ask her colleagues for guidance. This kind of careless and dismissive attitude regarding people’s health is far from professional.
